c.tagline: Olympic capital rising in terraces above Lake Geneva's vineyard shoreline.

taxi.fareNote: Taxis are metered and expensive by international standards; ranks are found at the station and Place St-Francois, or can be called/booked via app.

emergency.note: Emergency services are fast and reliable; English is widely understood by dispatchers and responders.

avoid.reason: Minor pickpocketing around the train station and the Flon nightlife district late on weekends.

hood_desc: Lausanne's lakefront district, with a promenade, marina and the Olympic Museum honoring the city's role as IOC headquarters. Popular for lakeside walks, boat trips and summer swimming.
A former industrial warehouse quarter reinvented as Lausanne's trendiest nightlife and shopping hub, packed with bars, boutiques and design offices.
The medieval hilltop core, dominated by the Gothic Lausanne Cathedral and cobbled streets leading to the Palais de Rumine and city museums.
The area around the main train station, convenient for transit connections, with a mix of budget hotels, cafes and everyday shops.

water.note: Tap water is excellent, including from public fountains.

transit.pay: Contactless card, mobiliz/Fairtiq app, or ticket machines at every stop
transit.note: Excellent integrated transit; Lausanne's m2 is Switzerland's only fully automated metro line, climbing steeply from Ouchy on the lake up to the old town and beyond.

train: Direct SBB/CFF trains to Geneva, Zurich, Bern and Paris (TGV Lyria), Milan
bus: Regional PostBus network to surrounding villages and vineyards
ferry: CGN paddle steamers and boats across Lake Geneva to Evian, Montreux and Geneva

tip.r: Service is included by law in restaurant prices; rounding up the bill or leaving small change for good service is appreciated but not obligatory.

places.name: Cafe du Grutli

places.name: Cafe Romand

food.name: Malakoff
food.desc: Deep-fried Gruyere cheese fritter served on a round of bread, a Vaud invention linked to soldiers back from the Crimean War.

places.name: Cafe du Grutli

places.name: A la Bossette

places.name: La Pinte Besson

places.name: La Pinte Besson

places.name: Cafe du Grutli

landmarks: Lausanne Cathedral (Notre-Dame)
Switzerland's finest Gothic cathedral, a 13th-century masterpiece with a glorious rose window and a night watchman who still calls the hours from its tower.
The Olympic Museum
The world's premier Olympic showcase in lakeside Ouchy, where torches, medals and interactive galleries celebrate the Games in the movement's capital city.
Ouchy Waterfront
Lausanne's Belle Époque lakefront of promenades, plane trees and paddle steamers, with the turreted Château d'Ouchy facing the Savoy Alps across Lake Geneva.
Place de la Palud
The medieval heart of the old town, where a 17th-century Fountain of Justice and an animated clock face the arcaded Renaissance town hall.
Palais de Rumine
A flamboyant Florentine-style palace on Place de la Riponne housing the cantonal museums of natural history, archaeology and coins.
Collection de l'Art Brut
Jean Dubuffet's revolutionary museum of 'outsider art', displaying raw, visionary works created by the self-taught, institutionalized and unclassifiable.
Escaliers du Marché
A covered wooden staircase of medieval origin zigzagging picturesquely from Place de la Palud up toward the cathedral terrace.
Sauvabelin Tower and Lake
A spiral wooden observation tower in the forested heights above town, overlooking a small boating lake and offering panoramas from Alps to Jura.
Plateforme 10
Lausanne's new arts district beside the station, uniting the cantonal fine-arts museum MCBA with photography museum Photo Elysée and design museum mudac.
Château Saint-Maire
A 15th-century castle built as the bishops' residence, now seat of the Vaud cantonal government, overlooking the old town from its hilltop grounds.

train.note: Lausanne station is a short metro ride above the lakefront at Ouchy. TGV Lyria reaches Paris in about 3h40, and EuroCity trains run to Milan via the Simplon. Domestically Geneva is 40 minutes away and Bern 70. The station has been under long-term reconstruction, so check platform arrangements. Swiss Supersaver fares open about two months ahead.

bus.note: Coaches stop near the station and at Ouchy. Switzerland's rail network makes domestic coaches largely redundant, though PostBus (https://www.postauto.ch/en) serves the mountain villages above the lake. Carry your passport or ID card for the French services.

intl.to: Évian-les-Bains & Thonon-les-Bains (France) - across Lake Geneva from Ouchy, ~35 min

ferry.note: The Évian crossing from Ouchy is a genuine international sailing and takes about 35 minutes, used by commuters as well as spa visitors - carry your passport. CGN's boats along the Swiss shore to Vevey, Montreux and the Chillon castle are covered by Swiss rail passes and are a lovely alternative to the train. Frequencies drop sharply outside April-October, and the paddle steamers run mainly in summer.

half.name: Lavaux Vineyard Terraces
half.blurb: UNESCO-listed vineyards cascading down to Lake Geneva just east of the city, laced with walking trails between wine villages like Lutry and Saint-Saphorin.
